claims.claim: `provan.change_brief.v1` has canonical structural validation and independently recomputed semantic validation.
`provan.affected_entity.v1` preserves typed entity identity, scope, state, authority, and evidence references.
`provan.affected_relationship.v1` preserves typed endpoints, relation, authority, and supporting evidence.
`provan.context_record.v1` preserves source, scope, lifecycle, authority ceiling, citations, and case binding.
`provan.case_context_bundle.v1` contains only validated records for one case and explicitly reports omissions and limitations.
`provan.context_request.v1` canonically binds explicit files, aliases, journeys, case metadata, and their digests.
`provan.context_provider_result.v1` remains a bounded provider result and cannot become canonical proof or policy by itself.
`provan.promotion_decision.v1` binds a pure versioned policy result to traceable eligible triggers and unresolved proposals.
`provan.acceptance_seed.v1` is candidate-bound, provenance-preserving, and explicitly proposed.
`provan.change_topology.v1` is derived only from canonical typed entities and relationships and preserves edge authority.
`provan.model_usage_receipt.v1` records actual model mode, provider/model/prompt binding, calls, latency, and cost status without fabrication.
`provan.session_handoff.v1` canonically binds Session 10 baseline, outputs, proofs, limitations, and implementation state.
`provan.error.v1` provides stable typed, user-safe error envelopes without leaking sensitive material.
`provan.acceptance_preparation.v1` represents preparation only and never a confirmed Acceptance Contract or verdict.
Every major semantic contract is independently recomputed from serialized canonical artifacts rather than delegated to production construction logic.
Immutable explain mode requires and resolves exact full base/head commit identities.

Mutable explain mode analyses tracked changes, deletions, bounded non-ignored untracked files, and separately reported index state while excluding unread sensitive-file contents and remaining Acceptance-ineligible.
`provan explain` supports a bounded local Git working-tree input without executing or mutating it.
`provan explain` supports credential-free canonical public GitHub HTTPS input with pinned commits and bounded transport.
PR metadata resolution is host-bounded, identity-checked, size/time-limited, credential-free, and consistent with explicit base/head inputs.
Explain analysis is source-only and invokes no inspected-repository build, test, install, hook, filter, textconv, or external-diff behavior.
Explain preserves inspected-target worktree, index, refs, object state, and monitored write state.
Agent-reported, source-attributed product intent, source-established facts, model-reviewed implications, and unresolved claims remain distinct in canonical data and every renderer.
Affected entities retain derivation authority and cannot be promoted by model or provider assertion.
Affected relationships retain endpoint, evidence, and authority bindings and cannot be promoted by model or provider assertion.
Unsupported dynamic, generated, reflective, runtime-only, or otherwise unqualified surfaces are reported as unresolved or noncoverage.
The bundled `CaseLocalContextProvider` executes only against explicitly supplied case-local inputs.
Every applied context source has a content fingerprint, citation, source type, and traceable case-local reference.
Case-local context cannot persist into or contaminate an unrelated case.
Provider output cannot self-declare owner confirmation, approved policy, runtime proof, execution proof, or stronger evidence authority.
Context providers cannot mutate the candidate, target, canonical Brief facts, policy, evidence classes, or storage outside the case boundary.
`community.default.v1` evaluates validated facts through a pure, deterministic, versioned PromotionPolicy.
A supported high-risk trigger promotes only when its exact deterministic rule and minimum canonical authority are satisfied.
A change with no supported eligible trigger remains `explain_only`.
Unsupported model-, prose-, or context-proposed triggers remain unresolved and cannot create mandatory policy.
Community policy cannot emit authoritative `acceptance_required_by_policy` without a separately qualified authority contract.
PromotionPolicy cannot modify Brief facts, evidence classes, entities, relationships, or context authority.
Every generated Acceptance Seed remains status `proposed` and preserves candidate, evidence, context, policy, and unresolved-question provenance.
A mutable Change Brief cannot become an Acceptance-eligible seed or preparation packet.
Promotion policy ID, version, decision, trigger refs, and reason refs survive into the Acceptance Seed and preparation packet.
`provan acceptance promote` creates preparation only and performs no confirmation, execution, challenge, clearance, or verdict operation.
Public, client-safe, rendered, and preparation artifacts contain no exact future challenge input, seed, selector weight, sibling, private oracle, or private eval material.
Change topology renders only when objective complexity rules are met and always provides an authority-preserving text/table fallback.
Terminal, JSON, Markdown, and offline HTML renderers preserve claim classes, evidence refs, limitations, and one bounded next action.

Cache reuse is limited to independently revalidated case-neutral repository-analysis fragments, while every case-bound Brief, context bundle, promotion decision, Seed, and model envelope is freshly constructed for its own case.
`--no-model` produces a usable deterministic Brief with exactly zero model calls and zero model egress.
Default/model-provider behavior uses at most one call only through an explicitly operator-configured and Provan-allowlisted provider and otherwise falls back deterministically.
Every attempted model use is bound to an exact usage receipt with honest reported, estimated, unavailable, or not-applicable status.
Inputs exceeding declared analysis or model limits produce explicit bounded limitations rather than silent truncation or fabricated completeness.
Internal, public, and client-safe projections preserve sensitivity boundaries and client-safe summaries are deterministically sanitised unless separately approved.
The Community runtime exposes no inspected-repository execution or mutation capability through any Session 10 command, adapter, provider, output, or cache path.
Session 10 exposes no verifier execution, verifier qualification, or runtime-behaviour verification capability.
Session 10 creates or executes no challenge pack, private challenge instance, sibling, oracle, or challenge verdict.
Session 10 creates no Enterprise workspace, persistent organisation memory, governed organisation policy, or arbitrary Enterprise provider runtime.
Private planning authority is absent from tracked history delta, package, public proof, examples, and controlled CI artifacts, as recorded by a generic non-sensitive absence result.
The authoritative Session 10 wheel installs in isolation and its documented CLI, doctor, explain, promotion, rendering, and cleanup paths work from site-packages.
Package `0.3.0` is bound to the Session 10 implementation as an unpublished `QUALIFIED_BOUNDED` main-tree capability and is not represented as a public release.
All accepted Session 9 schemas, historical artifacts, safety invariants, tests, and proof bindings remain preserved and valid.
Gate 10 real-use evidence is generated or replayed from the final reviewed implementation tree or its authoritative installed wheel.
Real-use comparison uses only the predeclared authentic PR body/review or existing public reviewer evidence and never a post-result synthetic comparator.
Every consequential Session 10 production range is dogfooded with provan explain and rerun after any production repair.
Every canonical Session 10 artifact remains under Provan-owned state, has content-addressed manifest bindings, and is independently resolvable by digest.
Community runtime and wheel have no dependency on provan-enterprise, provan-evals, private fixtures, or founder-local state.

Previous-Brief comparison accepts only canonical IDs or self-contained validated manifest-backed Provan exports, requires compatible repository lineage, and contributes no current evidence or authority.

The Session 11 handoff independently resolves every required candidate, Brief, entity, relationship, context, promotion, seed, addressing, projection, limitation, prerequisite, proof, reviewer, implementation, package, and schema binding without redesigning Session 10 semantics.

`provan.model_input_envelope.v1` binds the complete semantic model payload, including exact instructions and every selected block, to candidate, provider, model, prompt version, limits, and permitted output authority.
Literal and file CLI inputs are selected by distinct options and never reinterpreted through filesystem existence.
Explicit user-journey inputs remain case-supplied/source-attributed proposals and free-text or model-derived journeys never become owner-confirmed authority.

A model adapter transports only the envelope-declared semantic instructions and selected blocks, may add only provider framing metadata, and cannot add undisclosed source, context, retrieval, or prompt material.
Every explicit file option uses one bounded regular-file reader with type, size, encoding, containment, symlink, and reparse protections.
Case-supplied Brief text remains source-attributed product intent and cannot become owner-confirmed Acceptance authority in Session 10.

additive_claim_rule: Any new material implementation claim must be appended contiguously beginning at G10-72.
